events.description: An authorized S3 team member executed a command intended to remove a small number of servers for an S3 billing-related subsystem, but an input was entered incorrectly and a larger set of servers was removed than intended.
Removal of a significant portion of capacity caused the index and placement subsystems to require full restarts, and S3 became unable to service requests.
Other AWS services in US-EAST-1 relying on S3 were impacted, including the S3 console, EC2 new instance launches, EBS volumes needing S3 snapshot data, and AWS Lambda.
The restart and metadata integrity safety checks took longer than expected; the index subsystem was restarted first.
The team could not update individual service status on the AWS Service Health Dashboard due to a dependency on S3; status was communicated via the @AWSCloud Twitter feed and SHD banner text.
The team regained the ability to update individual services' status on the Service Health Dashboard.
The index subsystem activated enough capacity to begin servicing S3 GET, LIST, and DELETE requests.
The index subsystem was fully recovered and GET, LIST, and DELETE APIs were functioning normally.

events.time: February 28, 2017, after index subsystem was functional (before 1:54PM PST)

events.description: The placement subsystem finished recovery and S3 was operating normally.
Other impacted AWS services began recovering, with some requiring additional time to work through accumulated backlogs.
